record.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. In September 2025 the finance minister said the ruling Unity Labour Party would set out an AI policy in its election manifesto. The party's 2025 manifesto proposed AI-SVG, a national AI policy to be implemented in its next term, but the Unity Labour Party lost the November 2025 general election, in which the New Democratic Party won 14 of the 15 seats. No government AI policy, law or regulator has been found since.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. The retrieved material does not sufficiently establish the national AI governance arrangements. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.
Recorded the AI-SVG proposal in the Unity Labour Party's 2025 manifesto, without inferring government adoption; status unchanged. No new search or full recheck.
Recorded the November 2025 general election result and one English-language search for a government AI policy or body since; none found. Not a full recheck.

Re-ran searches in English for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified; results described the new minister's digital transformation portfolio, public-service cybersecurity training and selection for the World Bank's Digital LAC AI Accelerator. Kept low: the earlier AI policy was a defeated party's manifesto, and the new government's pages do not mention AI. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.language_note: English is an official language or an official language of national administration; it is a practical national search language for this check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. Preserved result batches, using 1-based positions in check.searches: VC-search = searches 1, 2 (en, en). Each multi-query batch has only a combined returned result set; its source_ids cannot be attributed to individual queries. Historical query dates are recorded as 17 October 2026 in the phase6 search-boundary ledger. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.

record.notes: The retrieved policy discussion concerns a party manifesto. A separate search of gov.vc returned AI use and training material but no second substantive official account of national AI governance or evaluation. English-language searches for a government-designated AI safety institute with a remit to evaluate advanced models included a separate search of gov.vc.
